title: Sense Organs Working Together
subject: Science
lessonFocus: The eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin work together to help us do tasks and stay safe.

review.job: help us see colors, shapes, people, food, and things around us.
help us hear sounds and warning signals.
helps us smell things, enjoy food, and notice warning smells such as smoke.
helps us feel by touch, such as the feathers of a bird or the surface of an object.

sections.title: Guided Practice
sections.subtitle: Let’s warm up! Choose the sense organ or organs that fit the situation.

questions.q: When you eat food, which sense organs work together?
questions.explain: Your eyes see the food, your nose smells it, and your tongue tastes it.

questions.q: When reading a book, which sense organ do you mainly use?
questions.explain: Your eyes help you see the words and pictures.

questions.q: When you listen to a story, which sense organ helps you hear it?
questions.explain: Your ears help you hear sounds.

questions.q: When you touch a bird’s feathers, which sense organ helps you feel them?
questions.explain: Your skin helps you feel things by touch.

questions.q: When you smell smoke, which sense organ gives you a warning?
questions.explain: Your nose helps you smell smoke and notice a possible danger.

sections.title: Practice
sections.subtitle: Think about how different sense organs work together.

questions.q: When crossing a street, which two sense organs work together to help keep you safe?
questions.explain: Your eyes help you see vehicles and signals, while your ears help you hear vehicle sounds.

questions.q: When buying a piece of cloth, which two sense organs can help you?
questions.explain: Your eyes can see the cloth, and your skin can feel its texture.

questions.q: When playing a guitar, which three sense organs from the lesson can be used?
questions.explain: You can see the guitar, hear the music, and feel the instrument with your skin.

questions.q: When cooking, which sense organs are used to smell and taste the food?
questions.explain: The nose smells the food and the tongue tastes it.

questions.q: When receiving a gift from a friend, which sense organ helps you hear what your friend says?
questions.explain: Your ears help you listen to sounds.

sections.title: Match It
sections.subtitle: Match each situation with the sense organ that helps most.

sections.title: Real-Life Science
sections.subtitle: Choose the answer that best explains how sense organs work together.

questions.q: Ana is eating a meal. Her eyes see the food, her nose smells it, and her tongue tastes it. What does this show?
questions.explain: Different sense organs can work together during the same activity.

questions.q: Ben hears a loud vehicle while crossing the street. Why are his ears useful?
choices: They help him notice sounds that can warn him.
They help him taste the vehicle.
questions.explain: Hearing sounds can give us warning signals.

questions.q: Mia smells smoke and looks around to find where it is coming from. Which sense organs are working together?
questions.explain: The nose detects the smell and the eyes help look for its source.

questions.q: A child touches a rough fruit and looks at its shape. Which sense organs are being used?
questions.explain: Skin helps feel the surface and eyes help see the shape.

questions.q: Why are sense organs important?
choices: They help us learn about our surroundings and do tasks safely.
They are only used when eating.
They are used only for playing.
questions.explain: Sense organs help us see, hear, smell, taste, feel, and respond to what is around us.

sections.title: Thinking Challenge
sections.subtitle: Choose the best answer. Think carefully!

questions.q: Which activity uses eyes, nose, and tongue together?
questions.explain: During eating, the eyes see the food, the nose smells it, and the tongue tastes it.

questions.q: Which activity uses eyes and ears together to help keep you safe?
questions.explain: When crossing, you can see vehicles and signals and hear vehicle sounds.

questions.q: Which pair can help you identify something when your eyes are closed?
questions.explain: The nose can smell things and the skin can feel objects.

questions.q: A child hears music and moves to the rhythm. Which sense organ helps hear the music?
questions.explain: Ears receive sounds such as music.

questions.q: Which statement is true?
choices: Different sense organs can work together during one activity.
Only one sense organ can work at a time.
Sense organs are not important for safety.
questions.explain: The lesson shows many activities in which two or more sense organs work together.
